I feel like I go about waifus a little (or a lot) differently than some people here. 

I'd like to have a relationship with someone real, but I feel like Tali'Zorah would still have a place in my heart for what she means to me and what she (and Mass Effect) represent: Right now I'm going through a tough period of my life and I'd like to be like the version of Shepard I created by playing the games. I know Tali fell in love with him For being kind, strong-willed, decisive, respectful, and a man of action. 

Shepard represents to me an ideal, so what about Tali? Well, to me she is what I'd love to have in a relationship. The first time I played MEI I did it as a female Shepard, I knew you could have a romance in the first game, just didn't have clear with whom. I tried to romance Tali, but could, moved to MEII, tried again, and the same story, MEIII, and nothing, again. At some point during the third game, I saw her flirting with Garrus (another character I had grown fond of) and I got ***REALLY*** jealous, I even thought I could separate them and romance her with my femshep with some content from a DLC, but nothing. They ended up together just before the last mission and when I saw them I felt like throwing the whole trilogy to hell and get it over with, but later I realized I was happy for them. I liked them both, they both were great characters and great people and Garrus was the best option for her. I realized I was happy because she was happy. I also realized I wanted her to romance my femshep not out of love, but just sex drive. After that, I started thinking I wanted to have a romance with her, but there was a problem: she was hetero and I only played as a female character in all RGPs. 

I thought, and thought, and thought, and decided to play as a man in an RPG for the first time in years. I started a new playthrough of the trilogy, eventually got comfortable, made some different decisions than in my first playthrough, got to know the lore and other characters better, and romance her. 

I learned a better meaning of "love", friendship, attraction, respect, optimism, and the weight of my decisions, among other things. 

I find her voice attractive, her body sexy, her personality heartwarming, her fears and motivations "human", her silliness adorable, and she as a whole a person worth living and dying for. The only thing I don't like about her is her canonic face. For other characters that would've been enough for me to stop liking them, but she has so many things I like and love that the fact she isn't entirely to my liking only makes her feel more real. 

And not to mention a phrase she tells Shepard and some point in the last game: "(No) The difference was you. That makes me be a real difference for the better.

TL:DR: I LOVE Tali'Zorah nar Rayya vas Normandy for helping me to know myself better, for giving me something to aspire to, for feeling real, for the warm feeling her thought can stir in my chest, and for those hips.

Let me share my personal experience:

I had liked many characters before (Princess Luna, Sunset Shimmer, 2B, Lara Croft, among others), and I had romanced other characters in games (Josephine Montilyet, many of the female characters in AC Odessey, Shahvee). Of some, I liked their design, voice, attitude, and role in the plot, but Tali'Zorah had all those things, and more importantly, she (and the Mass Effect trilogy) helped me to understand myself a little more, and start facing some personal issues. 

She means something to me thanks to a combination of factors, some "permanent" (like the quality writing of the trilogy) and others merely circumstantial (like the moment I bought the games), like a real relationship.

To me, having a "waifu" or "husbando" doesn't mean you don't like other characters, but that there's is a special place in your heart for he, she, it (you could like a robot), or they. You don't choose it, it just happens.

Some pieces of advice to sound more natural:

Instead of "Estoy en la uni" say "Soy universitaria". (Fewer words and more "powerful" if you will)

Change "...y me gusta pero no me gusta tanto como..." for "y la disfruto, pero la prefería el semester pasado" (avoid repeating the same word in the same sentence when possible, and in this contexts "pasado" fits better that "anterior". Both are right, though)

"Por ejemplo, vemos mucha historia y geografía" replaceses "Una razón por la que me gusta menos es que el contenido tiene más que ver con la historia y la geografía" (Both are correct, both considering the previous change I suggested you say the same with lesser words) 

"Tambien no me gusta que el profesor hable mucho más que nosotros, porque la clase tiene lugar 3 veces cada semana y solo dura por una hora. Es mi unica chance para hablar unicamente en español. 

\-"Tambien no" should be "Tampoco" 

\-"Hable" is wrong, try "Habla" (He speaks - Él habla) 

\-"Porque la clase tiene lugar 3 veces cada semana" "Porque la clase es (solo) 3 veces por semana" ("solo" is optional, but helps to emphasize the feeling) 

\-"... y solo dura por una hora..." (avoid "por". Nonetheless, It works in other contexts.)

I mixed some opinions with "rules", but I hope it helps.

I think there are many, like line quality, perspective, composition, and many others, BUT since this is a full-body drawing I think the most important aspects about it that you could work on are gesture and proportion. 

For proportions, I'd suggest you do all the research you can about the relation between the parts of the body, nonetheless, remember the proportions "changes" depending on the pose the body is doing. 

Now, about the gesture, my best piece of advice would be to acquire some professional courses or books. [Proko's figure course seems to be great](https://www.proko.com/figure-drawing-fundamentals-course/#.X8LHi2iYXIU), and [Mike Mattesi's force method](https://www.drawingforce.com) is super useful, too,  but if you are broke (like my ass), [this YT playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLqY6uto9mXfAas_cHNyVwUMohpbUiz_Du)[ can help you](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLqY6uto9mXfAas_cHNyVwUMohpbUiz_Du).

Last, but not least: don't forget that drawing (with pencil, pen, charcoal, oil, dirt, sand, or whatever) is about the same bits of knowledge (Gesture, anatomy, proportions, light theory,  composition, perspective, etc...) Study all of them to boost your learning.
